conventions.date_precision: kept as stated by the source; a year is never 1 January
conventions.year_end_observations: a fiscal year-end date (31 March) dates the statement, not the transaction, unless the note says otherwise

events.title: Dunhill Development Corporation Ltd. incorporated (No. 73385)

evidence.locator: British Columbia Gazette, 1976, Companies Act notice No. 73385

events.interpretation_notes: A private company: the Province did not own it until 1974.

events.title: Agreement under which the Province acquired Dunhill shares through Woodbridge Development Corporation

evidence.locator: Public Accounts 1974/75, F55, note 1 (round-4 claim R4E-C001)

events.interpretation_notes: The date the financial statements report for the agreement; the executed agreement has not been recovered.

events.title: Dunhill becomes a provincial Crown corporation

evidence.locator: Public Accounts 1975/76, F104, note 5 (round-4 claim R4E-C002)

events.interpretation_notes: The Province, through Woodbridge, held enough shares for Crown tax exemption. Not an incorporation date, nor proof of direct 100 per cent ownership on that day.

events.title: Dunhill wholly owned by the Province directly, after Woodbridge was wound up

evidence.locator: Public Accounts 1974/75, F55, note 1 (round-4 claim R4E-C003)

events.interpretation_notes: Not Woodbridge’s legal dissolution date.

events.title: Eight wholly owned Dunhill subsidiaries listed

evidence.locator: Public Accounts 1974/75, F55, note 2(a)(i) (round-4 claim R4E-C004)

events.interpretation_notes: W.K.P. Construction; Crown Lumber; Fisher Developments; Dunhill Homes; Dunhill Holdings; United Provincial Investments; Ventures Realty; Georgia Park Holdings. An observation at the year end, not when each was acquired.

events.title: Order in Council authorizes the Province’s proxy to pass the resolution renaming Dunhill
events.interpretation_notes: An authorization, not the rename: the name changed on 18 November. Taken from the research package of 2026-11-22; not re-read during integration (see VERIFICATION.md).

events.title: Dunhill Development Corporation Ltd. renamed Housing Corporation of British Columbia

evidence.locator: British Columbia Gazette, 1976, Companies Act notice No. 73385

events.title: Housing Corporation of British Columbia in voluntary liquidation

evidence.locator: Public Accounts 1984/85, note 9(h) (PDF p. 21)

events.interpretation_notes: Observed at the year end: its operations were in voluntary liquidation and its investment carried at $1 pending dissolution. When the liquidation began is not given.

events.title: Housing Corporation of British Columbia struck off the register and dissolved

evidence.locator: British Columbia Gazette, June 1990, Registrar of Companies’ notice under section 282 of the Company Act (PDF p. 9), No. 73385

events.title: Housing Corporation sells its real-estate sales subsidiary, Venture Realty Ltd., and part of its professional services division

evidence.locator: Public Accounts 1978/79, F154, Housing Corporation of British Columbia, note 1 (PDF p. 472); also Provincial Government Enterprise Finance 1978, printed p. 26

events.interpretation_notes: Effective 30 November 1978, a subsequent event in statements for the year ended 31 October 1978. Probably Ventures Realty Ltd. of the 1974 list; the spelling differs and no company number links them.

events.title: W.K.P. Construction Ltd. incorporated (No. 91003)

evidence.locator: British Columbia Gazette, 1976, Companies Act notice No. 91003

events.interpretation_notes: A private company; first shown in the Province’s group in 1974.

events.title: W.K.P. Construction Ltd. renamed Dunhill Development Corporation

evidence.locator: British Columbia Gazette, 1976, Companies Act notice No. 91003

events.interpretation_notes: A different company from the original Dunhill (No. 73385), which had become the Housing Corporation of British Columbia eight days earlier.

events.title: Dunhill Development Corporation (No. 91003, formerly W.K.P. Construction) struck off and dissolved

evidence.locator: British Columbia Gazette, June 1989, Registrar of Companies’ notice under section 282 of the Company Act (PDF p. 11)

events.title: T.S. Holdings Ltd. incorporated (year as Statistics Canada reports it)

evidence.locator: Provincial Government Enterprise Finance 1976, printed p. 22 (PDF p. 24), year column

events.interpretation_notes: The year only; the day is not known. Read by the verified research package of 2026-11-22; not re-read during integration.

events.title: The Province acquires bus companies through T.S. Holdings

evidence.locator: Provincial Government Enterprise Finance 1975, printed p. 27

events.interpretation_notes: Statistics Canada: it held shares in companies running scheduled bus routes, sightseeing and charter services and regional transit. Its own statements name them (see the 1976 roster event). Read by the verified research package of 2026-11-22; not re-read during integration.

events.title: Auditor’s report on T.S. Holdings Ltd. and subsidiary companies tabled in the Legislature

evidence.locator: Hansard, 25 January 1977, night sitting, opening proceedings

events.interpretation_notes: Tabled with the report on the administration of the Transit Services Act. The tabled report itself, which would name the subsidiaries, has not been found.

events.title: Auditor General reports operating losses at T.S. Holdings and a material receivable from Pacific Coach Lines

evidence.locator: Auditor General Report 1979, printed p. 17, paragraph 5.19

events.interpretation_notes: A debt between them, not ownership. Taken from the research package of 2026-11-22; not re-read during integration (see VERIFICATION.md).

events.title: T.S. Holdings’ $2,850,538 of advances cleared by a return of assets and a provision for doubtful recoveries

evidence.locator: Public Accounts 1979/80, printed B4 (PDF p. 172) and B8 (PDF p. 176)

events.interpretation_notes: $38,815 returned and $2,811,723 provided for. Its one share stayed on the books at $1: an accounting provision, not a dissolution.

events.title: Province holds Pacific Coach Lines’ entire issued capital, two common shares

evidence.locator: Public Accounts 1979/80, printed B4 (PDF p. 172)

events.interpretation_notes: Held directly, not through T.S. Holdings. Its $1,088,204 of advances were provided for as doubtful in the same year.

events.title: Pacific Coach Lines’ operations cease; wind-up begins

evidence.locator: Public Accounts 1984/85, note 9(i) (PDF p. 21)

events.interpretation_notes: After the budget of 7 July 1983 announced that the private sector would take over functions not appropriate to government.

events.title: The Province buys all of Panco Poultry’s common and preferred shares for $4,800,000

evidence.locator: Public Accounts 1978/79, F215, Surrey Farm Products Investments Ltd., note 3; month, price and subsidiaries also in Provincial Government Enterprise Finance 1975, printed p. 27 (PDF p. 29)

events.interpretation_notes: With its subsidiaries B.C. Testing Farms, Pacific Hatching and Western Feeds. The purchase made the company exempt from income tax.

events.title: Surrey Farm Products Investments shown as British Columbia Food Exhibitions Ltd., organizing Food Pacific 86

evidence.locator: Public Accounts 1984/85, Appendix II (PDF p. 7) and note 9(c) (PDF p. 20)

events.interpretation_notes: Now reported on a fully consolidated basis because its activities had changed.

events.title: Province holds 100 per cent of I.O.K. Poultry Ltd., 600 common shares

evidence.locator: Public Accounts 1977/78, printed B4 (PDF p. 72), 1977 and 1978 columns

events.title: I.O.K. Poultry Ltd. dissolved; $600 of proceeds recorded

evidence.locator: Public Accounts 1979/80, printed B8 (PDF p. 176): proceeds on dissolution

events.interpretation_notes: By this year end, not on it: the day of dissolution is not printed.

events.title: Crown Development Corporation wound up; its $1,000 of shares written off

evidence.locator: Public Accounts 1977/78, printed B8 (PDF p. 76)

events.interpretation_notes: By this year end, not on it: the day is not printed.

events.title: Panco Poultry Ltd. sells its business and assets for $12,076,253

evidence.locator: Public Accounts 1978/79, F215, notes 2–3

events.interpretation_notes: Net proceeds $11,724,660 after $351,593 of disbursements, a $9,010,630 gain over the assets’ net cost. A sale of the business, not of the company, which was renamed Surrey Farm Products Investments sixteen days later.

events.title: Surrey Farm Products Investments pays the Province a $14.8 million dividend

evidence.locator: Public Accounts 1978/79, F215, note 4 (subsequent events)

events.interpretation_notes: The Province’s $4.8 million investment was written down to $1 in 1979/80 as a return of capital. The revenue schedule’s “Sale of assets of Surrey Farm Products Ltd.”, $14,800,000, is this dividend under a shortened name, not the sale price.

events.title: Surrey Farm Products Hatchery Ltd. and Western Feed Co. Ltd. wound up

evidence.locator: Public Accounts 1984/85, vol. 3, G55, British Columbia Food Exhibitions Ltd., note 1 (PDF p. 61)

events.interpretation_notes: During the year ending 31 March 1985. Probably Panco’s Pacific Hatching (later Pacific Hatchery) and Western Feeds of 1975, but the spellings are not linked by a company number. A winding-up, not a registry dissolution.

events.title: British Columbia Food Exhibitions Ltd. (No. 63265, formerly Panco Poultry) struck off and dissolved under the Company Act

evidence.locator: British Columbia Gazette, 9 July 1992, printed p. 840 (PDF p. 8), Dissolutions, June 19, 1992

events.interpretation_notes: Under section 281 or 282 of the Company Act. No source read shows the Province still holding it after 1985.

events.title: Ministry of Municipal Affairs and Housing directs that the Housing Corporation’s operations be wound up

evidence.locator: Public Accounts 1978/79, F154, note 1 (PDF p. 472)

events.interpretation_notes: A directive to wind up operations, not a legal dissolution, which came in 1990.

events.title: Fisher Developments Ltd. incorporated (No. 71787)

evidence.locator: British Columbia Gazette, 16 December 1976, p. 1664, Companies Act notice No. 71787

events.interpretation_notes: A private company; first shown in the Province’s group in 1974.

events.title: Fisher Developments Ltd. renamed HCBC Construction Ltd.

evidence.locator: British Columbia Gazette, 16 December 1976, p. 1664, notice No. 71787

events.interpretation_notes: The same company: HCBC Construction is not a separate subsidiary.

events.title: Crown Lumber Limited sold at book value

evidence.locator: Public Accounts 1977/78, F152, Housing Corporation of British Columbia, note 1 (PDF p. 580)

events.interpretation_notes: The buyer is not named.

events.title: Dunhill Homes, Dunhill Holdings and Georgia Park Holdings wound up

evidence.locator: Public Accounts 1976/77, F133 (PDF p. 531)

events.interpretation_notes: Winding-up reported in the parent’s accounts, not registry dissolutions. Read by the verified research package of 2026-11-22; not re-read during integration.

events.title: T.S. Holdings’ wholly owned subsidiaries: V I T Holdings, Thompson-Okanagan Transit (formerly Tweed Line Tours) and Vancouver Island Transit (formerly McArthur Transportation)

evidence.locator: Public Accounts 1975/76, F176, T.S. Holdings Ltd. and subsidiary companies, note 1(a)

events.interpretation_notes: V I T Holdings in turn owned 98.24 per cent, directly or through a subsidiary, of Vancouver Island Transportation Company, Vancouver Island Coach Lines, Gray Line & Empress Taxi & Sightseeing, Imperial Charter Service and British Columbia Parlour Car Tours. The same subsidiaries are listed at 31 March 1977 (F202) and 1978 (F221).

events.title: V I T Holdings sells its 98.5 per cent of Vancouver Island Transportation Company Limited to the Province

evidence.locator: Public Accounts 1978/79, F223–F224, T.S. Holdings Ltd., note 6 (extraordinary item)

events.interpretation_notes: The Province bought the bus companies out of T.S. Holdings’ group as Pacific Coach Lines was formed; by 31 March 1979 T.S. Holdings held only Thompson-Okanagan Transit and Vancouver Island Transit.

events.title: Plan announced to replace Pacific Stage Lines and Vancouver Island Coach Lines with a new company

evidence.locator: BC Hydro annual report 1978/79, printed p. 10 (PDF p. 12)

events.interpretation_notes: The plan for the combined service; Pacific Coach Lines had already been incorporated and was operating on Vancouver Island. Read by the follow-up research package of 2026-11-22; not re-read during integration.

events.title: Crown Development Corporation incorporated, its shares held by the Attorney-General for the Crown

evidence.locator: Public Accounts 1975/76, F99, note 1 (PDF p. 485)

events.interpretation_notes: Incorporated under the Companies Act “to purchase and operate ships for ferry services, and to develop and manage crown land”.

events.title: British Columbia Cellulose Limited incorporated

evidence.locator: Public Accounts 1975/76, F8–F9, British Columbia Cellulose Company, note 1 (PDF p. 394)

events.title: British Columbia Cellulose Company Act assented to, continuing the company as a Crown corporation under that name

evidence.locator: SBC 1973 (1st Sess.) c. 8, ss. 1–2; Public Accounts 1975/76, F9, note 1

events.title: British Columbia Cellulose Company buys the last 2.5 per cent of Plateau Mills (225 shares, $191,250)

evidence.locator: Public Accounts 1975/76, F9, British Columbia Cellulose Company, note 2 (PDF p. 395)

events.interpretation_notes: The Province held the other 97.5 per cent directly: two public owners, not one.

events.title: Province acquires a majority interest in Plateau Mills (97 per cent as printed)

evidence.locator: Provincial Government Enterprise Finance 1973, printed p. 21, explanatory comments

events.interpretation_notes: As printed, 97 per cent, not the later 97.5. Read from the publication’s text only; the page image was not inspected. Read by the verified research package of 2026-11-22; not re-read during integration.

events.title: Plateau Mills, Kootenay Forest Products and 81 per cent of Canadian Cellulose transferred to the British Columbia Resources Investment Corporation

evidence.locator: Hansard, 10 April 1978, afternoon, budget address, printed p. 264; agreement approved by OIC 530/1978

events.interpretation_notes: The Finance Minister’s account of the completed transfer gives the day. BCRIC was itself wholly provincial until its 1979 public share issue. Read by the follow-up research package of 2026-11-22; not re-read during integration.

events.title: British Columbia Cellulose Company Repeal Act assented to
events.interpretation_notes: It dissolved the company only when brought into force by regulation.

events.title: British Columbia Cellulose Company dissolved under the British Columbia Cellulose Company Repeal Act

evidence.locator: OIC 631/1986, approved 19 March 1986, effective 31 March 1986; Repeal Act s. 2; archived consolidation note: B.C. Reg. 49/86

events.interpretation_notes: The 1985/86 Public Accounts (A11, note 5(b)) describe the dissolution as effective 1 April 1986; that wording is kept as a separate assertion, and is unexplained.

events.title: Province holds 97.5 per cent of Plateau Mills Ltd., 8,775 common shares

evidence.locator: Public Accounts 1977/78, printed B4 (PDF p. 72), 1977 column only: $7,663,256

events.interpretation_notes: Listed with the Crown corporations; British Columbia Cellulose Company held the other 2.5 per cent.

events.title: Province advances $50,000 to Thompson-Okanagan Transit Ltd.

evidence.locator: Public Accounts 1979/80, printed B4 (PDF p. 172) and B8 (PDF p. 176)

events.interpretation_notes: Issued during the year. An advance to a company T.S. Holdings owned: funding, recorded apart from ownership.

events.title: T.S. Holdings Ltd. struck from the Register of Companies

evidence.locator: Public Accounts 1980/81, printed B17, note 9(e) (PDF p. 201)

events.interpretation_notes: The remaining assets went to the Province, the sole shareholder, in satisfaction of share capital and retained earnings on the same date. The Public Accounts do not identify the statutory route.

events.title: Thompson-Okanagan Transit Ltd. dissolved

evidence.locator: Public Accounts 1980/81, printed B17, note 9(f) (PDF p. 201)

events.interpretation_notes: The company repaid its $50,000 provincial advance upon dissolution. This is separate from the removal of T.S. Holdings and does not establish an endpoint for Vancouver Island Transit Ltd.

events.title: Pacific Coach Lines Limited incorporated (No. 178561)

evidence.locator: Public Accounts 1978/79, F190, note 1 (PDF p. 508)

events.interpretation_notes: Two $1 shares issued; the source does not say who first subscribed for them. The Province is shown holding both at 31 March 1979.

events.title: Pacific Coach Lines buys the assets of Vancouver Island Transportation Company and begins operating

evidence.locator: Public Accounts 1978/79, F190, note 1 (PDF p. 508)

events.interpretation_notes: It had been inactive since incorporation. The Province had bought Vancouver Island Transportation Company from V I T Holdings on 24 July 1978.

events.title: Pacific Coach Lines takes over Pacific Stage Lines’ assets and operating responsibilities

evidence.locator: Public Accounts 1978/79, F193, note 9 (PDF p. 511); BC Hydro annual report 1978/79, printed p. 10

events.interpretation_notes: Not its first operations: it had run Vancouver Island services since 31 August 1978.

events.title: Province holds Pacific Coach Lines’ entire issued capital, two common shares

evidence.locator: Public Accounts 1978/79, B4 (PDF p. 34)

events.interpretation_notes: Read by the follow-up research package of 2026-11-22; not re-read during integration.

events.title: Pacific Coach Lines Limited (No. 178561) renamed 178561 B.C. Ltd.

evidence.locator: British Columbia Gazette, 2 August 1990, printed pp. 1083–1084 (PDF pp. 11–12)

events.interpretation_notes: The same week Royal Victorian Holdings Corporation (No. 362538) took the name Pacific Coach Lines Ltd. and Pacific Coach Lines (1984) Ltd. (No. 273925) became 273925 B.C. Ltd.: three companies. The rename does not show the Province still owned No. 178561.

events.title: 178561 B.C. Ltd. (formerly Pacific Coach Lines Limited) struck from the register and dissolved

evidence.locator: British Columbia Gazette, vol. 133, no. 24, 17 June 1993, printed p. 786, right column (PDF p. 10), Dissolutions, No. 178561 under 11 June 1993

events.interpretation_notes: The legal end follows the cessation of bus operations on 31 March 1984 and the change to the numbered name on 19 July 1990. The notice gives no evidence about ownership at dissolution.

events.title: V I T Holdings Ltd. liquidated

evidence.locator: Public Accounts 1978/79, F224, T.S. Holdings Ltd., note 6 (PDF p. 542)

events.interpretation_notes: A loss of $456,620 on liquidation. Its registry dissolution is not traced.

events.title: Panco Poultry Ltd. formed by amalgamation (No. 63265)

evidence.locator: British Columbia Gazette, 8 March 1979, printed p. 386, Companies Act notice No. 63265

events.interpretation_notes: A private company: the Province bought it in 1975.

events.title: Panco Poultry Ltd. renamed Surrey Farm Products Investments Ltd.

evidence.locator: British Columbia Gazette, 8 March 1979, printed p. 386, notice No. 63265

events.interpretation_notes: The same day Pacific Hatchery Ltd. (No. 64184, incorporated 12 April 1965) became Surrey Farm Products Hatchery Ltd. The later rename to British Columbia Food Exhibitions Ltd. is undated: after 14 February 1979 and by 17 June 1985.

events.title: Venture Realty Ltd. (No. 83729) renamed Venture Realty Consultants Ltd.

evidence.locator: British Columbia Gazette, 10 May 1979, printed p. 776

events.interpretation_notes: After the Housing Corporation sold it. Incorporated 30 December 1968. Nothing links No. 83729 to the 1974 list’s plural “Ventures Realty Ltd.” Read by the follow-up research package of 2026-11-22; not re-read during integration.

events.title: British Columbia Cellulose Company acquires 79 per cent of Canadian Cellulose Company, Limited

evidence.locator: Public Accounts 1975/76, F9 and F94 (PDF pp. 395, 480)

events.interpretation_notes: A majority, not a wholly owned subsidiary, so Canadian Cellulose is not drawn. The same day certain assets and liabilities of Columbia Cellulose Company, Limited were combined with Canadian Cellulose’s: two companies, not a rename. Read by the follow-up research package of 2026-11-22; not re-read during integration.

events.title: British Columbia Cellulose Company buys all the shares of Kootenay Forest Products Ltd. from Eddy Match

evidence.locator: Public Accounts 1975/76, F128, note 1 (PDF p. 514)

events.interpretation_notes: Effective that day. The company also bought the assets and third-party liabilities of Eddy Match’s Kootenay Forest Products and Stafford Mills divisions for $8,768,390, advanced by BC Cellulose.

events.title: British Columbia Cellulose Company declares a specie dividend to the Province of all its Canadian Cellulose, Kootenay Forest Products and Plateau Mills shares

evidence.locator: Public Accounts 1977/78, F23, British Columbia Cellulose Company, notes to the 1977 statements, note 10 (subsequent events); also its 1978 statements, note 3 (Public Accounts 1978/79, F24)

events.interpretation_notes: The same day the Province transferred the shares to BCRIC; the Province’s advances to BC Cellulose, $19,849,421 with interest, were forgiven. The Province added its own 278,100 Canadian Cellulose shares, making the 81 per cent it transferred.

events.title: OIC 631/1986 approved, bringing the repeal into force on 31 March 1986

evidence.locator: OIC 631/1986 (B.C. Reg. 49/86), one-page original

events.interpretation_notes: Approval, not commencement: the order takes effect on 31 March 1986.

events.title: Canadian Cellulose, Kootenay Forest Products and Plateau Mills amalgamated into a new Canadian Cellulose Company, Limited

evidence.locator: BCRIC Annual Report 1980, note 14, printed p. 25 (PDF p. 27)

events.interpretation_notes: After public ownership: BCRIC’s 1979 share issue had taken the companies out of the Province’s hands. The successor reused Canadian Cellulose’s name but is a new company. Read by the follow-up research package of 2026-11-22; not re-read during integration.

events.title: Province holds 40 per cent of Swan Valley Foods Ltd.

evidence.locator: Public Accounts 1977/78, printed B5 (PDF p. 73), 1977 column: 219,804 common and 28,266 preferred shares, $425,501

events.interpretation_notes: Listed under Investments, Other, not with the Crown corporations. The Court of Appeal says the government at one point owned more than 40 per cent.

events.title: Creston Valley Foods Ltd. buys Swan Valley’s Creston plant, equipment and technology for a $1.5 million debenture

evidence.locator: Swan Valley Foods Ltd. (Creston Valley Foods Ltd.) v. Assessment Appeal Board, BC Court of Appeal, 1 May 1980, pp. 1–2

events.interpretation_notes: Creston Valley Foods was newly incorporated for the purchase and owned through Federal Diversiplex by Hardee Farms International: a different company, not Swan Valley renamed. Swan Valley assigned the debenture to the Province, which carried it at $1 (Auditor General 1978, para. 8C.15).

events.title: Province buys more Swan Valley shares before selling them: $7,631,250 in cash and $251,000 for waiving interest

evidence.locator: Public Accounts 1977/78, printed B8 (PDF p. 76)

events.interpretation_notes: In the year ending 31 March 1978 and before the sale on 1 December 1977; the days are not printed. Explains why the buyer bought 100 per cent from the Province when it had held 40 per cent.

events.title: Province sells all of Swan Valley Foods’ shares and certain debentures to Standard Brands Limited for $2,200,000

evidence.locator: Standard Brands Limited, Annual Report 1977, note 6 “Acquisition” (printed p. 30, PDF p. 33)

events.interpretation_notes: The Province’s accounts give the consideration as a $2,000,000 promissory note and cash held in trust, and write off the $8,307,751 book value of the shares (Public Accounts 1977/78, B8). Standard Brands’ own note 5(d) carries the $2,000,000 note.

events.title: Swan Valley Foods Ltd. continued from British Columbia under the Canada Business Corporations Act (No. 026524-1)

evidence.locator: Corporations Canada, Swan Valley Foods Ltd., corporate history: certificate of continuance

events.interpretation_notes: A continuance, not a new incorporation.

events.title: Swan Valley Foods Ltd. amalgamated into Standard Brands Canada Limited

evidence.locator: Corporations Canada, corporation 298239: name history (Standard Brands Canada Limited from 1978-04-28 to 1982-05-12) and amalgamation certificate

events.interpretation_notes: The registry lists the result under its later name, Nabisco Brands Canada Ltd. (from 1982), itself amalgamated on 1987-03-29.
